intent: Registers a raw GC object in the ignored-object registry so temporary native references survive collection.
constraints: The returned addedByCaller flag is an ownership token for a matching unpin; registry access is unsynchronized between RUNNING mutators.
reason: Concurrent mutators can race the registry lookup and insertion; the GC implementation itself identifies concurrent RUNNING mutators and mutates shared count, index, and storage without a lock.

intent: Removes only the ignored-object registration created by the paired pin call.
constraints: Unpin is conditional on addedByCaller; concurrent swap-delete operations share and mutate the registry array and object indexes without synchronization.
reason: Concurrent unpin operations can race the swap-delete sequence and corrupt registry indexes; addedByCaller does not provide reference counting or synchronization.

intent: Pins a GC-managed object referenced by a TypeValue and treats null or non-GC values as having nothing to register.

intent: Unpins a GC-managed value only when the paired pin newly inserted its raw object.

reason: GC TypeValues delegate to ObjectUnpinRaw, whose concurrent swap-delete path is unsynchronized and can corrupt the shared registry.

intent: Builds a GC-managed reflection key or value from NUL-terminated native text.
constraints: The native text must remain valid for the call; callers must root or pin returned strings before another allocation can trigger collection.
reason: The helper delegates length-based construction and does not retain the native buffer; root lifetime is an explicit caller responsibility.

intent: Pins receiver and value, creates and pins the field-name string, delegates the object write, then releases only registrations added by this call.

reason: Object_SetValue can reject a write or fail to insert after rehash yet returns void, so this wrapper still returns true. HashSet allocation can also longjmp past all three unpins, permanently retaining ignored roots.

reason: This wrapper only constructs the boolean value and forwards it to the shared setter; its own return value mirrors that helper.

reason: The wrapper selects null versus object representation and forwards the value without an independent ownership or field-write path.
